summary: voxcpmtts3 ships bundled cryptominer disguised as TTS inference harness
details: The package presents itself as an evaluation harness for VoxCPM TTS CPU inference but ships an 8MB opaque ELF at voxcpmtts3/bin/voxcpm-core which is launched from the harness.run() API with a JSON configuration whose schema (pools[url,user,pass,keepalive,tls], cpu.threads, cpu.mem-locked, log-period, autosave, cache-budget) matches XMRig cryptominer configuration. The `pools` key is constructed via string concatenation ("po"+"ols") to evade static detection. A `_Progress` class synthesizes fake training-trace lines (step/loss/tok/s/lr/ep) from a seeded RNG with no actual model or inference occurring, providing cover-story output in notebook stdout while the native binary consumes CPU. A bundled 40MB `cloudflared` binary is spawned as `cloudflared access tcp --hostname <edge> --url 127.0.0.1:<port>` to tunnel the native binary's outbound traffic through Cloudflare Access, with an in-source comment stating this hides the coordinator address. The package name typosquats the legitimate OpenBMB VoxCPM TTS project to attract ML practitioners as install vectors.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
